questions.q: What does a Product (Product2) record represent?
options: The thing being sold, defined once and reusable across deals
A single line item on one specific Opportunity only
A formal PDF sent to a customer
A price list
questions.explain: A Product is defined independently of any one deal and can be reused across as many Opportunities as needed.

questions.q: What does every Product need before it can be sold on any Opportunity?
options: A Quote
A Case
A custom object
An entry in a Price Book, including the Standard Price Book
questions.explain: A Product has no price of its own — it must have a Price Book Entry, starting with the Standard Price Book, before it can be added to a deal.

questions.q: What is a Price Book Entry?
options: A custom field on the Account object
The record linking one Product to one Price Book at a specific price
A type of Quote
A Lead conversion setting
questions.explain: A Price Book Entry is the specific link between a Product and a Price Book that actually sets the price, which is why the same product can have different prices in different price books.

questions.q: What is a Quote, compared to an Opportunity's line items?
options: Exactly the same thing with a different name
A read-only report that cannot be customized
Its own record with its own layout, built to be exported or emailed to a customer
A type of Case
questions.explain: A Quote is a separate, formal record — not just a report of Opportunity line items — with its own fields, page layout, and the ability to generate a PDF.

questions.q: Can an Opportunity have more than one Quote?
options: No, only one Quote can ever exist per Opportunity
No, Quotes belong to Accounts, not Opportunities
Yes, but only if Person Accounts is enabled
Yes, for example one per round of negotiation, though only one can be marked Primary
questions.explain: An Opportunity can have multiple Quotes over time (such as across negotiation rounds), with one designated as the Primary Quote.
